Leonard Bernstein, born in 1918 and died in 1990, was a towering American composer, conductor, author, and pianist who was one of the most charismatic and influential figures in twentieth-century classical music. He served as the long-time music director of the New York Philharmonic and conducted many of the world's finest orchestras. As a composer, he effortlessly bridged the gap between serious classical genres and popular musical theater, writing symphonies, ballets, and acclaimed Broadway shows, most notably West Side Story.

West Side Story from 1957 is his legendary musical that updates Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet to nineteen fifties gang rivalry in Manhattan between the Jets and the Sharks, featuring lyrics by Stephen Sondheim. Candide from 1956 is an operetta based on Voltaire's satirical novella, celebrated for its virtuosic overture and the notoriously difficult coloratura soprano aria Glitter and Be Gay. His Symphony No. 2, The Age of Anxiety from 1949, is a symphonic work for orchestra and solo piano based on the Pulitzer Prize-winning poem of the same name by W. H. Auden. Chichester Psalms from 1965 is a three-movement choral work setting Hebrew Psalm texts, scored for mixed choir, boy soprano or countertenor, organ, harp, and percussion. On the Town from 1944 is his first hit Broadway musical, expanding on his ballet Fancy Free, which follows three sailors on a twenty-four-hour shore leave in New York City and includes the song New York, New York. Young People's Concerts was a series of fifty-three televised concert lectures with the New York Philharmonic that introduced millions of children to classical music and music theory between nineteen fifty-eight and nineteen seventy-two.

Bernstein was a central icon of mid-century American classical music and music education. He was a close lifelong friend and disciple of Aaron Copland, conducting and recording the definitive performances of Copland's orchestral works. He collaborated closely with Stephen Sondheim on West Side Story, launching Sondheim's professional Broadway career.
